title: Frontend: Sum of Consecutive Integers
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Sum of Consecutive Integers. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(n) for a positive safe integer. Count representations as sums of one or more consecutive positive integers. Return the count; reject nonpositive/noninteger values with Invalid n.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
For a sequence length k, subtract k(k-1)/2 from the target and require the remainder to be a positive multiple of k.
alternativeApproaches: Return each starting value and length, and relate the count to odd divisors under the same positivity assumptions.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Target one; power of two; odd target.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
